_README: THESE THREE DEALS ARE HYPOTHETICAL. Every figure was invented to demonstrate
the calibration method. They are NOT real transactions, NOT market data, and
NOTHING should be concluded about Atlas's accuracy from them.
Copy this file to calibration/deals.json and replace it with deals you
actually know the outcome of. Three is the minimum that shows a pattern;
it is not enough to prove one.
'inputs' is what you would have entered in Atlas BEFORE the deal.
'actual' is what really happened. actual_profit must be on the same basis
as the executed strategy: an exit profit for wholesale and flip, an annual
cash flow for buy & hold, BRRRR and seller finance.

deals.name: HYPOTHETICAL 1 — flip where the ARV came in low
deals.description: Underwritten at a $250k ARV from three comps; sold for $232k after sitting an extra two months, and lost money.

actual.notes: Sold below the underwritten ARV and took two extra months. A $2,500 buyer credit at closing is not modelled by Atlas and shows up as the residual.

deals.name: HYPOTHETICAL 2 — wholesale assignment that held up
deals.description: Contracted at $78k against a $205k ARV. Assigned, but for less than the model said the spread supported.

actual.notes: Assignment closed at $11,000 against a modelled $14,739. The buyer's own rehab number was higher than ours, and they negotiated the fee down.

deals.name: HYPOTHETICAL 3 — rental where the expenses were understated
deals.description: Bought as a hold. Rent came in as expected, operating costs did not.

actual.notes: Annual cash flow, not exit profit. Rent came in slightly under, and a first-year roof repair exceeded the maintenance reserve.
